scope: Independent follow-up window after cancellation-priority and 45-second fallback deployment. Earlier samples and pre-followup files are excluded.

deployment.source: Parent official deployment result and next invocation cutoff.

healthAndLeaseEvidence.interpretation: Owner changes are anonymized invocation evidence. collector_status.expiresAt is heartbeat expiry, not the actual lease TTL. These files do not prove final lease release or rule out an unobserved lease interruption.

cancellationEvidence.note: Guard records are checkpoint observations, not a counter of all cancellation attempts. request_cancelled is a pre-HTTP guard; snapshots alone cannot distinguish runtime-budget exhaustion from every lease/probe guard condition.

limitations: All targets, owners, stores, SKUs and token identifiers are omitted. Group and invocation numbers are stable only within this report.
Whole-window counts report progress between snapshots. They are distinct from strict interval statistics, whose earlier and later recorded anchors both must be at or after 13:33:00Z.

For a multi-request segment, an earlier lastRequestAt at or after the cutoff proves all subsequently recorded request intervals start after it. The same rule separately applies to successful-result anchors. Otherwise the entire metric segment is excluded from strict means.
Exact single intervals require exactly one counter increment and both timestamp endpoints after the cutoff. Spans covering multiple requests/successes are never treated as one interval.
Known-single extrema cover only recoverable individual intervals. Lifetime maxMs, snapshot polling gaps and aggregate count/sumMs cannot reconstruct a window p95 or whole-window extrema.

Request timestamps are scheduler dispatch times. Success timestamps include the upstream outcome transaction. Durable equality confirms that corresponding success was saved, not all intermediate stage timings.
Guard absence at six snapshots cannot rule out a transient denial between polls. Per-target inFlight and exact runtime deadline are not retained in checkpoints.
Per-invocation stats reset and are neither summed nor differenced. Sender readiness does not establish receipt of a real phone notification.

Passing the freshness threshold is not evidence that every interval meets the 60-second target. The configured work budget is not persisted in these snapshots and must be established by deployed source/version evidence.
